text:
Barrett Hayton has spent most of his career being measured against the fifth overall pick he was in 2018. This season the better measure is what happens when he's on the ice. Utah has 63.8% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five in his 14:48 a night, nearly ten points better than when he sits. Evolving-Hockey liked his defense last season too, putting him in the 89th percentile among forwards at taking chances away.

His own scoring is lagging the process. He has three goals on 4.8 expected, shooting 7.7% against the 11.2% our numbers peg as his level. He has scored in two of his last four games, including the power-play goal against San Jose on Saturday that forced overtime, and with 11 points in 21 games he's already closing on last season's 25. What to watch is simple: whether the finishing catches up with shifts this good.
